- When sentiment is strongly positive (≥ 0.67) in recent days, model tends to overestimate prices; reduce forecast slightly to align with mean reversion.
- When sentiment is strongly negative (≤ 0.33) or shows sharp drops, model underestimates; adjust upward, especially if recent price is rising.
- After a sharp price spike (e.g., >5% from prior day), model often overshoots; cap forecast at 1–2% below peak or use lagged 3–5 day average as anchor.
- If sentiment shifts from negative to positive mid-horizon, model fails to catch momentum; increase forecast slope gradually, not abruptly.
- Model consistently underestimates in 30-day horizon when sentiment is mixed or volatile; add 0.5–1.5% buffer to forecast mean if sentiment variance > 0.3.
- If last 3–5 days show strong upward momentum, model often fails to reflect it; use 2x smoothing of recent highs for 10–15 day horizon.
- When sentiment is flat or neutral (0.00–0.33), model tends to drift toward prior mean; apply mean reversion correction with 1–2 day lag.
